title: Prepositions, purpose and verb + -ing
matching: Typed answers ignore letter case, extra spaces, apostrophe style and final . ! or ? punctuation. Accents and every other character count. Multiple-choice answers must match exactly.

lessons.title: Prepositions of time and place
lessons.explanation: Use at for clock times and exact points: at six o'clock, at the station. Use on for days and dates: on Monday, on 5 May. Use in for months, years, seasons and larger places: in July, in 2020, in winter, in London. For place, in means inside, on means touching a surface, and next to or between show position: The keys are on the table. The shop is next to the bank.

examples.en: The class starts at nine o'clock.
The keys are on the table.

lessons.title: Infinitive of purpose
lessons.explanation: Use to plus the base verb to say why someone does something: I went to the shop to buy milk. She is studying to become a nurse. This answers the question Why? and means the same as in order to. Do not use for followed directly by a base verb: not I went to the shop for buy milk. Use for plus a noun if you like: I went to the shop for milk.

She is studying to become a nurse.

lessons.title: Verb + -ing patterns
lessons.explanation: After some verbs and after prepositions use the -ing form: I enjoy swimming. She finished writing. We are interested in learning Spanish. He is good at cooking. Enjoy and finish take -ing. Like, love, hate and start can take either -ing or a to-infinitive; stop to do something has a different meaning from stop doing it. After a preposition always use -ing: thank you for helping, before leaving. After enjoy, do not use the base verb or a to-infinitive: not I enjoy to swim.
